brief.headline: Aluminium closed the week back above its $3,077 pivot: Friday's LME official lifted three-month $16 to $3,080 and cash $43 to $3,114, widening the backwardation to $34 - the tightest prompt signal since mid-September - as LME stock fell to another low and European gas broke above EUR 100/MWh.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: Friday's LME official (the weekly close) settled cash at $3,114.00 (+$43.00) and three-month at $3,080.00 (+$16.00, +0.52%), up $62 on the week. Cash now trades $34.00 above three-month (backwardation), up from $7.00, and LME stock fell 475 t to a new low of 231,200 t. Aluminium outperformed copper and nickel, which fell.

WHY: prompt metal is scarce on the LME (eight straight stock draws), and the smelter cost floor rose again - European gas topped EUR 100/MWh for the first time since late 2022 and Brent rose above $113 on renewed US-Iran strike concern (Trading Economics). December-hike odds eased to about 72% from about 83% as a tech sell-off pulled bond yields lower.

AGAINST: the close is only $3 above $3,077 and the spread has crossed the $15 tightness line four times in six sessions; SMM expects ex-China output to return to year-on-year growth in November as Middle East capacity restarts, and Chinese output stays near record.

WHAT TO WATCH: Monday's official - a second close above $3,077 with the backwardation above $15 would strengthen the bullish case, a close below $3,061.5 would weaken it; Chalco's Q3 report (still not located); Hormuz incidents (Iranian claims of tanker fires remain unconfirmed).

lme.commentary: WEEKLY CLOSE ABOVE 3,077. On the Friday 30-October official cash settled $3,114.00 (+$43.00) and three-month $3,080.00 (+$16.00), regaining 3,077 one session after losing it and closing the week $62.00 higher at the first weekly settlement above the 3,077 50% retracement. Cash led the rise, so the backwardation widened to $34.00 from $7.00 - the widest in the sequence since mid-September and back above the $15.00 reversal condition, with spread and price both stronger; visible stock fell 475 t to a new low of 231,200 t. Aluminium was among the firmer metals on the board (aluminium +0.52%, lead +0.58%, zinc +0.26%, copper -0.70%, nickel -0.80%). Macro was mixed: a tech-led sell-off pulled the US ten-year toward seven-week lows (about 4.93%) and eased December-hike odds to about 72% from about 83%, while European gas broke above EUR 100/MWh for the first time since late 2022 and Brent rose above $113 on renewed US-Iran strike concern (Trading Economics, 30-October). SMM reports ex-China October aluminium output 1.2% lower y/y but expects a return to growth in November as Middle East capacity restarts. September's official means were cash $3,276.82 and three-month $3,272.89. The structure has flipped across $15.00 four times in six sessions, so Monday's official is the persistence test.

drivers.text: The Q4 Japanese premium has settled 35% lower, at $255/t — SETTLED: Reuters (07-October) reported that some Japanese buyers agreed to pay $255/t over LME cash for October-December shipments, down 35% from $395/t in Q3 and below producers' initial offers of $310-325/t; producers named in the talks included Rio Tinto and South32, and talks with other buyers were ongoing. A Japanese trading-house source cited recovering Middle East output after the March attacks on Gulf smelters and rising Indonesian shipments. Negotiations ran longer than usual because of a wide gap between the two sides. The settlement sits inside the $245-260/t offer range AL Circle reported on 06-October, and above CRU's $202/t Asia CIF assessment. WHY IT MATTERS: the quarterly MJP is the reference for much Asian physical business, so the regional premium level resets about $140/t lower for the quarter.
drivers.source: Reuters via LSE.co.uk - Some Japanese aluminium buyers agree to pay Q4 premiums of $255/t, 35% lower than Q3 (07-Oct-2026)

drivers.text: Spot premiums have fallen below the new quarterly benchmark - but sellers' pressure is easing — SMM's 09-October assessment puts CIF Japan MJP spot at $230/t, $25 beneath the $255/t Q4 quarterly settlement, with Korea at $216-223/t and Thailand at $249/t. SMM concludes the outlook for overseas premiums 'has become less bearish' and premiums may stabilise or recover modestly near term, but a stronger rebound needs clearer improvement in downstream orders and restocking. WHY IT MATTERS: with spot below the quarterly benchmark, remaining Japanese buyers have little reason to settle above $255/t, and the Q1-2027 talks start from a lower spot base.
drivers.source: SMM - Overseas primary aluminum premiums near a floor as selling pressure eases (09-Oct-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese primary imports fell 14.65% year on year in August, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China metal — Public customs data reported on 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports at 185,500 tonnes, DOWN 14.65% year on year and up just 0.16% month on month, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia (2,920 t), Indonesia (2,180 t) and Malaysia (1,800 t) accounting for almost all of the remainder. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED: domestic capacity is at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting is described as resilient, and inventory is being drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. WHY IT MATTERS FOR PREMIUMS EVEN SO: a premium is set by competition for units at a location. China importing 14.65% less primary metal, and 96% of what it does import arriving from a single discounted-origin supplier, means the marginal ex-China unit faces less Chinese competition - which works against premiums in Japan, Europe and the United States regardless of why Chinese buying fell.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China Aug aluminium imports down 14.7% year on year, Russia accounts for 96% of supply (25-September-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese semis exports hit a 2026 high, which pressures converter margins in exactly the markets where premiums are assessed — Public data reported on 25-September show China's August aluminium extrusion exports at 92,500 tonnes, the highest monthly figure of 2026, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 tonnes and 3.0% month on month from 89,800 tonnes, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER at 85,000-92,000 tonnes because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; the share of processing trade rose while ordinary trade fell, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE PREMIUM READ IS SPECIFIC: extrusions compete with locally converted metal in third markets. More Chinese semis arriving in South-East Asia, Africa and Latin America pressures the converter margins that ultimately support regional ingot premiums, even though the same exports support Chinese domestic ingot demand. The two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China's August aluminium extrusion exports hit a YTD high; pullback expected in September amid narrowing price spread (25-September-2026)

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: REVIEWED SATURDAY 10-OCTOBER-2026. Trading Economics' Brent coverage (09-October) says the US-Iran conflict continues to strain shipping: tankers are tied up in ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz, freight rates are at record highs and eleven tankers were attacked in the Strait in the week ending 04-October; President Trump said the US would not strike Iran again before the midterm elections. No container or bulk transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP pending a public, verifiable normalisation signal. PRIOR: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 30-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 29-September records the US rejecting Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, new US sanctions on 10 suppliers to Iran's military, and Tehran awaiting a formal US response to its ceasefire proposal; the Strait remains closed. Middle East crude exports reached 12.8 million b/d, the highest since February, but largely via ship-to-ship transfers and pipeline bypasses that do not serve Gulf aluminium exports. No transit count is published because tracker figures remain disputed. Arrow stays UP. PRIOR: REVIEWED TUESDAY 29-SEPTEMBER-2026. Public reporting on 28-September records indirect US-Iran talks resuming through mediators in New York, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed to commercial shipping; Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumed after drone-strike repairs, with flows reported near 3.5 million b/d, offering a partial bypass for crude but not for Gulf aluminium exports. Transit counts remain disputed between trackers and outlets, so no transit figure is published. Arrow stays UP until a dated, verifiable reopening step. PRIOR: REVIEWED MONDAY 28-SEPTEMBER-2026. On Saturday 26-September the US President publicly rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap - release of frozen funds, lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the naval blockade within four to five days, with the Strait reopened and negotiations under way by day seven - calling it not acceptable. He told reporters he expects talks to resume in the coming week; separately, US officials were reported as signalling a renewed bombing campaign after the November midterms. Iran's foreign minister said Tehran will not back down on its conditions and awaits mediators' formal feedback. Public tracking (straits.live, 27-September) classifies the Strait as closed to commercial traffic on day 210, with a pre-crisis baseline of about 85 transits a day; some outlets report sizeable US-escorted crude movements, so transit counts are DISPUTED and none is used as a figure here. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT SETTLED OUTCOMES. WHY THE ARROW GOES FROM FLAT BACK TO UP: last week's cut to flat rested on a visible negotiation; its latest proposal was publicly rejected and a post-midterm escalation path was reported. headlines.title: LME ALUMINIUM CLOSES THE WEEK ABOVE 3,077. The Friday 30-October official settled cash at $3,114.00 (+1.40%) and three-month at $3,080.00 (+0.52%), regaining 3,077 one session after losing it - the first weekly settlement above the 3,077 50% retracement, up $62.00 on the week. Visible stock fell 475 t to a new low of 231,200 t. Board: lead three-month +0.58%, aluminium +0.52%, zinc +0.26%, copper -0.70%, nickel -0.80%; copper built 1,800 t, the only stock build.

THE CURVE FIRMED WITH PRICE: the cash-to-three-month backwardation widened to $34.00 from $7.00 on 30-October, the widest in the sequence since mid-September and back above the $15.00 reversal condition, because cash rose more than three-month into month-end. READ: a twelfth straight backwardation, but the signal has crossed $15.00 four times in six sessions.

EUROPEAN GAS TOPS EUR 100/MWh (Trading Economics, 30-October): TTF rose about 6% to roughly EUR 103.6-104.0/MWh, the first time above EUR 100 since late 2022 and about 40% higher on the month; EU storage was 74.89% full on 29-October (Germany 61.65%, Netherlands 65.53%), about 100 TWh below last year, with Gulf LNG deliveries cut by Hormuz disruption and colder forecasts. Brent rose above $113, near the $116.72 four-year high of 23-October, on reports of US strike options against Iran and two tanker incidents in Hormuz. READ: the smelter energy-cost floor rose again.

HIKE ODDS EASE ON TECH SELL-OFF (Trading Economics, 30-October): weak results from major tech firms triggered a flight to safety that pulled the US ten-year toward seven-week lows (about 4.93%); CME FedWatch December-hike odds eased to about 72% from nearly 83% on 29-October; the dollar index held near 102, up about 0.5% in October.

EX-CHINA OUTPUT TO TURN POSITIVE (SMM feed, 30/31-October): October primary aluminium output outside China fell 1.2% y/y while average daily output rose 1.6% m/m; SMM expects November to return to positive y/y growth (+0.2%) on new capacity and production resumptions. SMM separately notes active buying but weak demand in the ex-China ingot market and rising selling from China's bonded zones. (Article pages returned 404; figures are from the feed summaries.)

YUNNAN ALUMINIUM NINE-MONTH PROFIT +164% (AL Circle, 31-October): revenue CNY 52.61bn (+19.4% y/y from CNY 44.07bn); net income CNY 11.6bn (+164% from CNY 4.39bn); basic EPS CNY 3.35 (from CNY 1.27). Q3 standalone figures and output were not given in the source.

AMAG NINE-MONTH EBITDA +59% (AL Circle, 30-October): 9M-2026 revenue EUR 1.3bn (+16.4%), EBITDA EUR 181m (from EUR 114m), net income EUR 82m (from EUR 34m), shipments 342,900 t (+7%); Q3 revenue EUR 473m (+35%), EBITDA EUR 80m on shipments of 121,500 t (+21%, including about 9,000 t carried over from Q2). Free cash flow was an outflow of EUR 67m; full-year EBITDA guidance EUR 200-220m.

NORTH AMERICAN DEMAND +3.5% IN H1-2026 (AL Circle, 30-October): demand grew 3.5% while domestic supply declined, with imports filling the gap - consistent with a tariff-inflated US Midwest premium that still has to attract imported metal.

RUSAL AND GHANA'S GIADEC PLAN A 5 Mt/yr BAUXITE MINE AND 1.2 Mt/yr ALUMINA REFINERY (AL Circle, 30-October) - a long-dated addition to ex-China raw-material supply; no timeline or financing is confirmed in the source.

HORMUZ REMAINS AN ACTIVE MARITIME EMERGENCY (Straits Daily Brief, 31-October): IMF PortWatch shows 2 transits on 25-October against an 85/day baseline; Al Jazeera reports Oman rescued 25 people from a burning tanker; Iranian claims of four tanker fires, a second captured US drone and a destroyed unmanned vessel are UNCONFIRMED. The brief's oil-price feed had no print, so no Brent level is taken from it.

LME ALUMINIUM GIVES BACK 3,077. The Thursday 29-October official settled cash at $3,071.00 (-0.97%) and three-month at $3,064.00 (-0.65%), ending a three-session rise one session after the first settled close above 3,077; three-month held $2.50 above 3,061.5. Visible stock still fell 225 t to a new low of 231,675 t. The board fell outside zinc: nickel three-month -1.27%, copper -0.93%, lead -0.88%, zinc +0.26%; copper posted the only stock build (+750 t).

THE CURVE SOFTENED WITH PRICE: the cash-to-three-month backwardation narrowed to $7.00 from $17.00 on 29-October, back below the $15.00 reversal condition one session after regaining it, because cash fell more than three-month. READ: still an eleventh straight backwardation, but the joint price-and-structure confirmation of 28-October lasted one session.

US DATA REVIVE DECEMBER-HIKE PRICING (Trading Economics, 30-October): Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annualised rate against 3.1% expected; September PCE inflation rose to 3.6% with core at 3.1%; initial jobless claims fell to 194,000. Traders price nearly 83% odds of a 25bp December hike after the Fed's 28-October hold. The US ten-year eased to about 4.92% and the dollar index to about 101.7. SMM's morning minutes (30-October) say resurfacing rate-hike expectations are pressuring the aluminium rebound.

CHINA INGOT INVENTORY FLAT (SMM, 30-October): three-region social aluminium ingot inventory was 409,000 t, unchanged day on day, with Gongyi down to 118,000 t and Guangdong (116,500 t) and Wuxi (174,500 t) up; SMM says inventories are still falling overall but destocking slowed mid-week and expects prices to consolidate short term.

VEDANTA Q2 FY27 (AL Circle, 29-October): group revenue INR 258.12bn (+57% y/y), EBITDA INR 99.38bn (+106%), PAT INR 62.02bn (+151%); Vedanta Aluminium EBITDA INR 101.92bn (+83% from INR 55.82bn) at a 46% margin, on record quarterly aluminium output of 649 kt (+5% y/y, +3% q/q) and alumina 895 kt (+37%).

CONSTELLIUM RAISES 2026 GUIDANCE (AL Circle, 29-October; reported 28-October): Q3-2026 revenue $2.64bn (from $2.17bn), adjusted EBITDA $276m (from $235m), net income $119m (from $88m) on shipments of 368 kt, slightly lower y/y; 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance now $1.03-1.06bn excluding metal price lag, free cash flow above $300m.

ENERGY RE-FIRMS (Trading Economics / Straits Daily Brief, 30-October): TTF rose to about EUR 99.85/MWh (+1.97%, up about 35% on the month) on colder forecasts and EU storage below 75%; Brent near four-year highs on concern US strikes on Iran could resume ($115.50 at 00:04 UTC per the Straits brief). Hormuz is still effectively closed (IMF PortWatch: 2 transits on 25-October vs an 85/day baseline); an IRGC claim that tankers struck mines is unconfirmed by any maritime authority. READ: smelter energy costs stay elevated.

ALUMINA PRICES DOWN 22% Y/Y (AL Circle, 29-October, citing Nanshan's unaudited nine-month disclosure): overseas alumina prices averaged around $321/t in January-September 2026, about 22% below a year earlier, low in H1 and recovering in Q3 on new overseas smelting capacity and some refinery constraints.

LME ALUMINIUM CLEARS 3,077. The Wednesday 28-October official settled cash at $3,101.00 (+0.75%) and three-month at $3,084.00 (+0.65%) - a third straight rise, the highest three-month settlement since 09-October and the first settled close above 3,077. Visible stock fell 200 t to a new low of 231,900 t. Every metal on the board rose: zinc three-month +1.04%, nickel +0.64%, copper +0.34%, lead +0.31%; stocks fell for all five.

THE CURVE FOLLOWED THIS TIME: the cash-to-three-month backwardation widened to $17.00 from $14.00 on 28-October, back above the $15.00 reversal condition one session after slipping below it, because cash rose more than three-month. READ: the first session in this rebound where prompt tightness and flat price confirmed together - one session, not yet a trend.

Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD TEST ON THE PAGE, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE WHERE THIS PAGE HAS NAMED THE MECHANISM IN ADVANCE. The 118,000-tonne two-week destock to 24-September is attributed by its own source to pre-holiday stockpiling and a widening spot-futures spread. Both drivers reverse by design once the holiday ends: stockpiled metal is consumed rather than bought, and the spread normalises. If Chinese inventory rebuilds sharply in the first two weeks of October, the single strongest bullish number on this page will have been a calendar effect; if it does not rebuild, the destock was demand and the deficit case strengthens materially. That is a genuine binary and it resolves in mid-October. THE SIX-YEAR RECORD SETS THE YARDSTICK (SMM via AL Circle, 26-September): across 2020-2025 ingot inventory rose 4% to 17.3% over the holiday week and total inventory 6.9% to 21.2%. A rebuild at the bottom of that band would confirm the pre-holiday destock as demand; a rebuild at or above the top would mark it as timing.

THE NEXT WEEKLY ALUMINA, FLUORIDE AND SILICON PRINTS. SMM publishes its alumina index, national alumina operating rate, fluoride salt review and silicon industry review on Thursdays, so 01-October is the next scheduled refresh for four rows of this page that are currently carried at 24-September: the alumina index at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne, the operating rate at 76.89% on 119.62 Mt/y, aluminium fluoride at 11,500-12,500 and cryolite at 8,300-9,000. The number to watch is the alumina index: the alumina-to-metal ratio at 11.13% against a decade norm of 15-17% is what underwrites this year's producer earnings, and a rising Chinese index is the mechanism by which that normalises.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND ITS RELEVANCE IS AT ITS HIGHEST OF THIS CYCLE. The US ten-year Treasury yield printed 5.214% on the 25-September reference session, a further multi-year high, and financing cost is the most persistent bearish input on this page. WHAT MAKES THIS MEETING MORE INTERESTING THAN USUAL: on the same session that the yield made a further high, the aluminium contango NARROWED $11.50. If the curve can tighten against a rising rate, then the rate is a headwind rather than the determinant, and the October meeting will test which of those two descriptions is right.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE. Prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle on monthly cycles concluding around the 17th-18th. The September cycle has printed and is carried - anodes at about 5,730 yuan/tonne, pitch at about 4,960, calcined petroleum coke at $470-525/t - and the October cycle is the next scheduled refresh for those three rows. Carbon is roughly 22-28% of smelter cash cost in aggregate across the anode, pitch and coke lines, so it is the second-largest block after power and alumina, and it is the block where this page has the least frequent data.

The last dated development is 07-September reporting of Iran describing an arrangement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping as days away, after more than three weeks of talks; nothing has been signed, and the stated US timetable still falls after the November midterms. A signed and implemented arrangement is the single largest bearish event available to this page, because it would unwind the Gulf supply premium that a substantial part of the 2026 price level rests on. THE CHINESE TRADE PULL IS RAISED TO UP AS A NEW NAMED RISK, AND IT IS THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE NEW FUNDAMENTAL INFORMATION IN THIS WINDOW. Customs data reported 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports DOWN 14.65% year on year at 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total; net imports 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67%; January-August 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. On the same day August extrusion exports printed a 2026 HIGH of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with September guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing price spread. The stated cause of the import fall is structural - capacity at the 45-million-tonne ceiling, resilient end-use demand, inventory drawn down through semis exports - but the effect on the ex-China balance is identical whatever the cause: less Chinese competition for ex-China primary units and more Chinese semis competing with Western fabricators. THIS DIRECTLY WEAKENS THE LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION OF THE EX-CHINA DEFICIT CASE.
